_meta.scope: US sellers, full returns where the item comes back (partial refunds are v2)
_meta._note: Keys beginning with _ are NOTES for the owner and are NEVER shown or used in math. Edit the numbers here when a platform changes fees; re-check quarterly. The 'refund' object is the DEFAULT/conservative policy; the calculator's 'what happened' selector overrides it for eBay.

ebay.label: eBay
ebay._note: eBay US 2026: 13.6% final value fee on MOST categories (books 15.3%, trading cards/coins 13.25%) on the part up to $7,500, then 2.35%. Per-order fee is $0.30 for orders of $10 or less and $0.40 above $10 — the calculator computes this from the sale price, no extra field. There is NO separate payment-processing fee (it's bundled). On a return the fee CREDIT depends on the reason: a buyer-remorse refund (changed mind / doesn't fit) credits everything INCLUDING the per-order fee; a 'not as described / damaged / wrong item' refund credits the 13.6% but KEEPS the per-order fee; if eBay stepped in and ruled against you, or you refunded outside eBay, you get NO credit at all. The 'what happened' selector drives this. The $20 dispute fee applies to chargebacks you lose — surfaced in the note/FAQ, not the core math.

poshmark.label: Poshmark
poshmark._note: Poshmark 2026: 20% commission on sales of $15+, or a flat $2.95 under $15; buyer pays $6.49 flat shipping; no recurring fees. On an approved 'not as described' return your commission is reversed and Poshmark gives a prepaid return label, so you usually pay $0 in fees and $0 in return shipping — your real loss is the ITEM'S VALUE if it comes back worn/damaged. Fit / change-of-mind returns now run through Seel (Worry-Free Returns): Seel refunds the buyer, the item goes to Seel's warehouse, and you KEEP your earnings — those cost you nothing. Overweight label upgrades (5–10 lbs $5, 10–15 lbs $15) are deducted from earnings when YOU ship out, not on returns. Texas sellers pay an extra ~8.25% tax on the commission (since Oct 2025), also reversed on a return — note only, not modeled.

mercari.label: Mercari
mercari._note: Mercari US 2026: the selling fee is BACK — 10% of (item price + buyer-paid shipping) for listings created/updated on or after Jan 6, 2025. There is NO separate seller payment-processing fee (the 3.6% buyer-protection fee is on the BUYER). On an approved return under 50 lbs Mercari hands the buyer a prepaid return label, so you pay $0 return shipping; OVER 50 lbs (or over the size limit) YOU must provide and pay the return label within 3 days or the order is canceled — that is your Mercari shipping-loss line. The 10% selling fee is typically reversed on an approved return (sale reversed = fee reversed); if your real case differs, the 'what did the platform refund' fallback still protects the math. Cancellation fee (5%, max $25) and $3 Instant Pay are not return losses — ignored.

depop.label: Depop
depop._note: Depop US 2026: NO selling fee for US/UK/AUS sellers. Payment processing is 3.3% + $0.45 via Depop Payments (Stripe), charged on price + shipping + tax. Crucially, when you refund a buyer via Depop Payments, ALL fees (selling, processing, boosting) are reversed automatically — so on a return your fee loss is normally $0, and your real loss is the ITEM'S VALUE plus any return shipping. (PayPal sellers outside UK/US/AUS must raise a support ticket to recover the selling fee.) Boosted listings carry a 12% boosting fee (new listings from 23 Mar 2026), also refunded on a refund — note only. US buyers get a prepaid return label; buyers outside the US arrange their own tracked return, reimbursed up to $20; returns must ship within 7 days of being agreed.
